title: Phase 5: camera focus (D72)
intro: tests/midi/03_band.mid, 0-34 s, alto sax lead on channel 1 sung by Delay Lama (profile mode), the band 6 dB down as live. Rendered offline as live playback mixes it (live.wav). 'Focus on' replays a scripted camera move recorded from the real 3D scene (focus_timeline.csv; PNGs focus_*.png): camera 1A until 16 s, a glide in to 60 units from the choir's face (16-19.6 s), held until 24.4 s, a glide back out, 1A from 28 s. Round 2, after your answer to round 1 ('too small', +12 dB when near): the near choir now stands out by 12 dB. It rises 6 dB itself (+12 clipped the monks: 346 samples at full scale) and the other 6 dB come off everything else. Measured over the hold (19-25 s): monks +6.0 dB (peak -3.4 dBFS, no clipping), band -9.3 dB (bass, guitar, pad -21 dB; the drums, half in the picture, -2.1 dB); the monks stand 15.3 dB further out against the band than without focus. Outside the move the two files are identical.

tests.title: Camera focus on a sung choir (round 2: 12 dB)
tests.question: While the camera is close to the choir, does the mix follow it the way you want?
tests.notes: Loop 14-30 s to hear the move in and out. Listen for the size of the change and whether the glides (about a second) pump or click.
